🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 YC, SFI complain against police personnel over photos with accused

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 11:38:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Youth Congress and the Students Federation of India (SFI) have lodged separate complaints alleging that police officers were photographed with persons accused in serious criminal cases. The complaints were submitted to Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala and the Director General of Police (DGP).

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Youth Congress Kannur district president Vijil Mohanan filed a complaint against Jayesh, an officer attached to the Sreekandapuram police station, after a photograph purportedly showing the officer with the accused in a case involving an attack on a Sreekandapuram municipality councillor was circulated. The Youth Congress alleged that Jayesh had intervened to prevent the arrest of the accused until they secured anticipatory bail. Speaking to the media, Mr. Mohanan called for an inquiry and action against the officer over his alleged association with the accused. Jayesh is a former district office-bearer of the police association. Meanwhile, the SFI Kannur district committee approached the DGP seeking disciplinary action against two Kannur City police personnel for allegedly posing for photographs with Athul M.C., one of the accused in a case involving an alleged attempt to murder students of Nirmalagiri College, Koothuparamba, on September 4, 2026. In his complaint, SFI Kannur district committee secretary Joyal Thomas identified the personnel as civil police officers C. Nijin and Suresh Narikkottan, both attached to the Kannur City police district headquarters. The complaint stated that the photographs were subsequently circulated in various groups. Mr. Thomas said that maintaining friendly relations with people accused in serious criminal cases and circulating such photographs could undermine the dignity and impartiality of the police. He alleged that the conduct violated the Kerala Police Act, the Kerala Government Servants’ Conduct Rules and social media guidelines.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He said such conduct could affect investigations, weaken public confidence in the justice system and embolden accused persons. He called for a departmental inquiry and strict action against the officers for alleged dereliction of duty and indiscipline.

Municipality (Noun)
नगर पालिका — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Municipality' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Impartiality (Adjective / Verb)
निष्पक्षता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Impartiality' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Departmental (Adjective)
विभागीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Departmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Association (Noun)
संगठन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Association' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "YC, SFI complain against police personnel over photos with accused", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Youth Congress and the Students Federation of India (SFI) have lodged separate complaints alleging that police officers were photographed with...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'YC, SFI complain against police personnel over p' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'YC, SFI complain against police personnel ove' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'YC, SFI complain against police personnel ove' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Youth Congress and the Students Federation of India (SFI) have lodged separate complaints alleging that police officers were photographed with..." (Hinglish Arth: युवा कांग्रेस और स्टूडेंट्स फेडरेशन ऑफ इंडिया (एसएफआई) ने अलग-अलग शिकायतें दर्ज कराई हैं, जिसमें आरोप लगाया गया है कि पुलिस अधिकारियों ने गंभीर आपराधिक मामलों में आरोपी व्यक्तियों के साथ तस्वीरें खींची थीं।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "YC, SFI complain against police personnel over photos with accused"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. He called for a departmental inquiry and strict action against the officers for alleged dereliction of duty and indiscipline.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "He called for a departmental inquiry and strict action against the officers for alleged dereliction of duty and indiscipline." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कर्तव्य में कथित लापरवाही और अनुशासनहीनता के लिए अधिकारियों के खिलाफ विभागीय जांच और कड़ी कार्रवाई की मांग की।)

articles.title: Working class in India is mobilising and resisting attack from many fronts: World Federation of Trade Unions leader
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Pambis Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The general secretary of the World Federation of Trade Unions (WFTU), Pambis Kyritsis, on Friday said that the working class in India is mobilising and resisting the attack from the neoliberal government and capitalists from both within and outside the country that are shrinking their rights to promote work without protection. “The attack is from the neoliberal government, the four labour codes and capitalists of this country and outside to shrink rights and deny any collective bargaining and collective agreement. But what is encouraging is that we see a very effective alliance among working labour movement and agriculture,” he told presspersons here. Mr. Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday. Founded in 1945, post the World War II, the WFTU is present in more than 130 countries. In India, seven central trade unions are its affiliates. It represents more than 110 million workers all over the world and, through its seven affiliates, represents more than 20 million workers. Kyritsis said that the conference was taking place at a time when workers around the world are facing challenges of many kinds. He cited “the genocide of the Palestinian people in Gaza, the attacks against the population in the West Bank by the Israel Army and settlers, supported and encouraged by the United States, the European Union, and their allies, the attacks on Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, the crude attempt to strangle Cuba through illegal and immoral economic energy blockade, the intervention in Venezuela and the abduction of the country’s president.” More workers through their trade unions are resisting and refusing to work for the war, to work for the war economy, he added. Stating that Asia Pacific region is increasingly becoming a key focus of imperialist interests, he said, “The only encouraging and hopeful element within this depressing picture is that workers are not possibly accepting this anti-people and anti-worker attacks. Guided by class-oriented trade unions, millions of workers around the world are choosing the path of struggle, to defend their trade, union, social and political rights. Through million mobilisations, in every corner of the globe, they demand jobs with rights that ensure the satisfaction of their contemporary needs.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The union leader felt that the cost of living crisis — currently unfolding in Europe — is a universal phenomenon and not of one country or continent, and that increasing of prices is hurting much more the poor people. He also said that once the workers agitate at one place, it will have triggering effect on others in a global village when the impact is felt immediately elsewhere.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Working class in India is mobilising and resisting attack from many fronts: World Federation of Trade Unions leader

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 11:38:33 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Pambis Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The general secretary of the World Federation of Trade Unions (WFTU), Pambis Kyritsis, on Friday said that the working class in India is mobilising and resisting the attack from the neoliberal government and capitalists from both within and outside the country that are shrinking their rights to promote work without protection. “The attack is from the neoliberal government, the four labour codes and capitalists of this country and outside to shrink rights and deny any collective bargaining and collective agreement. But what is encouraging is that we see a very effective alliance among working labour movement and agriculture,” he told presspersons here. Mr. Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday. Founded in 1945, post the World War II, the WFTU is present in more than 130 countries. In India, seven central trade unions are its affiliates. It represents more than 110 million workers all over the world and, through its seven affiliates, represents more than 20 million workers. Kyritsis said that the conference was taking place at a time when workers around the world are facing challenges of many kinds. He cited “the genocide of the Palestinian people in Gaza, the attacks against the population in the West Bank by the Israel Army and settlers, supported and encouraged by the United States, the European Union, and their allies, the attacks on Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, the crude attempt to strangle Cuba through illegal and immoral economic energy blockade, the intervention in Venezuela and the abduction of the country’s president.” More workers through their trade unions are resisting and refusing to work for the war, to work for the war economy, he added. Stating that Asia Pacific region is increasingly becoming a key focus of imperialist interests, he said, “The only encouraging and hopeful element within this depressing picture is that workers are not possibly accepting this anti-people and anti-worker attacks. Guided by class-oriented trade unions, millions of workers around the world are choosing the path of struggle, to defend their trade, union, social and political rights. Through million mobilisations, in every corner of the globe, they demand jobs with rights that ensure the satisfaction of their contemporary needs.”

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Pambis Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The general secretary of the World Federation of Trade Unions (WFTU), Pambis Kyritsis, on Friday said that the working class in India is mobilising and resisting the attack from the neoliberal government and capitalists from both within and outside the country that are shrinking their rights to promote work without protection. “The attack is from the neoliberal government, the four labour codes and capitalists of this country and outside to shrink rights and deny any collective bargaining and collective agreement. But what is encouraging is that we see a very effective alliance among working labour movement and agriculture,” he told presspersons here. Mr. Kyritsis is in Bengaluru to participate in the two-day Asia Pacific region conference of the WFTU that commenced here from Friday. Founded in 1945, post the World War II, the WFTU is present in more than 130 countries. In India, seven central trade unions are its affiliates. It represents more than 110 million workers all over the world and, through its seven affiliates, represents more than 20 million workers. Kyritsis said that the conference was taking place at a time when workers around the world are facing challenges of many kinds. He cited “the genocide of the Palestinian people in Gaza, the attacks against the population in the West Bank by the Israel Army and settlers, supported and encouraged by the United States, the European Union, and their allies, the attacks on Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, the crude attempt to strangle Cuba through illegal and immoral economic energy blockade, the intervention in Venezuela and the abduction of the country’s president.” More workers through their trade unions are resisting and refusing to work for the war, to work for the war economy, he added. Stating that Asia Pacific region is increasingly becoming a key focus of imperialist interests, he said, “The only encouraging and hopeful element within this depressing picture is that workers are not possibly accepting this anti-people and anti-worker attacks. Guided by class-oriented trade unions, millions of workers around the world are choosing the path of struggle, to defend their trade, union, social and political rights. Through million mobilisations, in every corner of the globe, they demand jobs with rights that ensure the satisfaction of their contemporary needs.”
• 3. He also said that once the workers agitate at one place, it will have triggering effect on others in a global village when the impact is felt immediately elsewhere.

articles.title: Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the deepathoon at the Thirupparankundram Hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24). A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice. The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State. The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the deepathoon on the coming Karthigai Deepam day. The deepathoon (stone lamp pillar) is around 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. While the dargah is at the hilltop, the Subramaniya Swamy Temple is at the base of the hillock. The court’s interim arrangement comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the dargah on the ownership of the hilltop and the deepathoon site “What weighs with us at this stage is the peculiar nature of the occasion and the proximity of the festival, which is scheduled to take place on November 24. The opportunity to perform the ceremony on that particular day, if denied, cannot be restored by any subsequent adjudication. Equally, we are conscious that the performance of the ceremony, once permitted, cannot be undone,” said the order. The Bench, comprising Justice P.B. Varale, said there was a need to balance the immediacy of the festival with the need to ensure that the interim order would not prejudice the appeal of the State or become fodder for claims of a vested right. “We are of the view that a limited, one-time arrangement, subject to stringent safeguards, would appropriately balance the interests involved pending further consideration,” the court observed. Imposing a series of restrictions and safeguards, the court directed that the Subramaniya Swamy Temple Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24. It ordered that the composition and number of the team would be settled by the Madurai Collector in consultation with the temple’s Executive Officer, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Commissioner of Police, Madurai. The Collector would act as the nodal officer for the event. The Commissioner of the Madurai City Police has to provide the ring of security. The Centre was directed to supplement security arrangements with CRPF personnel, if required. The Bench banned any kind of procession, public congregation, demonstration, slogan-raising or activity extraneous to the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the site. The leeway given for November 24 should not be construed as a judicial recognition of an essential religious practice, the court emphasised repeatedly. “We make it abundantly clear that the present arrangement does not proceed upon any finding that the stone pillar is, or has historically been, a place of customary religious observance. Nor does it determine whether the lighting of the lamp at the location constitutes an essential religious practice or whether any individual, religious denomination or institution possesses an enforceable right in that regard. All questions concerning title, possession, customary usage, religious entitlement, temple administration, and access to the site are expressly left open,” the court underscored.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons. The team would immediately leave the spot of the ‘deepathoon’ after lighting the lamp without leaving behind any temporary or permanent installation or objects, the court ordered. No damage or change would be made to any religious monument, including the nearby dargah on the Hill, the interim order stated, adding that the access and enjoyment of worshippers to the dargah should not be disturbed.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Supreme Court allows lighting of lamp on deepathoon at Thirupparankundram as limited one-time arrangement

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 11:27:43 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Supreme Court on Friday (November 20, 2026) allowed the lighting of the lamp, as a “limited one-time arrangement”, on the deepathoon at the Thirupparankundram Hill in Tamil Nadu’s Madurai district on Karthigai Deepam day (November 24). A Bench headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, however, stayed the conclusive findings of the Madras High Court in a January 6 judgment that upheld the right to light the lamp on the deepathoon as an essential practice. The court issued notice on the appeals filed by the State. The interim order dealt with pleas by the State to stay the January 6 judgment and looked into the question whether the lamp could be lit on the deepathoon on the coming Karthigai Deepam day. The deepathoon (stone lamp pillar) is around 50 metres from the Sikandar Badusha Dargah. While the dargah is at the hilltop, the Subramaniya Swamy Temple is at the base of the hillock. The court’s interim arrangement comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the dargah on the ownership of the hilltop and the deepathoon site “What weighs with us at this stage is the peculiar nature of the occasion and the proximity of the festival, which is scheduled to take place on November 24. The opportunity to perform the ceremony on that particular day, if denied, cannot be restored by any subsequent adjudication. Equally, we are conscious that the performance of the ceremony, once permitted, cannot be undone,” said the order. The Bench, comprising Justice P.B. Varale, said there was a need to balance the immediacy of the festival with the need to ensure that the interim order would not prejudice the appeal of the State or become fodder for claims of a vested right. “We are of the view that a limited, one-time arrangement, subject to stringent safeguards, would appropriately balance the interests involved pending further consideration,” the court observed. Imposing a series of restrictions and safeguards, the court directed that the Subramaniya Swamy Temple Devasthanam would exclusively decide the members of the team to light the lamp on November 24. It ordered that the composition and number of the team would be settled by the Madurai Collector in consultation with the temple’s Executive Officer, the Archaeological Survey of India, and the Commissioner of Police, Madurai. The Collector would act as the nodal officer for the event. The Commissioner of the Madurai City Police has to provide the ring of security. The Centre was directed to supplement security arrangements with CRPF personnel, if required. The Bench banned any kind of procession, public congregation, demonstration, slogan-raising or activity extraneous to the ceremonial lighting of the lamp at the site. The leeway given for November 24 should not be construed as a judicial recognition of an essential religious practice, the court emphasised repeatedly. “We make it abundantly clear that the present arrangement does not proceed upon any finding that the stone pillar is, or has historically been, a place of customary religious observance. Nor does it determine whether the lighting of the lamp at the location constitutes an essential religious practice or whether any individual, religious denomination or institution possesses an enforceable right in that regard. All questions concerning title, possession, customary usage, religious entitlement, temple administration, and access to the site are expressly left open,” the court underscored.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons. The team would immediately leave the spot of the ‘deepathoon’ after lighting the lamp without leaving behind any temporary or permanent installation or objects, the court ordered. No damage or change would be made to any religious monument, including the nearby dargah on the Hill, the interim order stated, adding that the access and enjoyment of worshippers to the dargah should not be disturbed.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Archaeological (Adjective)
पुरातत्व — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Archaeological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Nor does it determine whether the lighting of the lamp at the location constitutes an essential religious practice or whether any individual, religious denomination or institution possesses an enforceable right in that regard. All questions concerning title, possession, customary usage, religious entitlement, temple administration, and access to the site are expressly left open,” the court underscored.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The access to lamp-lighting would be allowed to only authorised persons. The team would immediately leave the spot of the ‘deepathoon’ after lighting the lamp without leaving behind any temporary or permanent installation or objects, the court ordered. No damage or change would be made to any religious monument, including the nearby dargah on the Hill, the interim order stated, adding that the access and enjoyment of worshippers to the dargah should not be disturbed.

articles.title: Messi visit row: Keralam govt. grants sanction to investigate former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The State government on Friday issued orders to accord sanction under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, to investigate former Minister for Sports, Minority Welfare and Waqf, V. Abdurahiman, along with two other former officials, over the alleged financial and procedural irregularities linked to the aborted visit of the Argentina national football team to the State. According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation. Alongside Mr. Abdurahiman, who has been named as the third accused in the case, the government has sanctioned probes against his former private secretary C. Sathyapalan, and former Kerala State Sports Council president U. Sharafali, who are the fourth and fifth accused respectively. The order follows a formal request from the State Police Chief based on a preliminary report submitted by the SIT. The government observed that an independent perusal of the SIT’s findings disclosed a prima facie case warranting an investigation into recommendations made and decisions taken by the former Minister and the officials during their tenure. The government had earlier received sanction from the Keralam Lok Bhavan to prosecute the former Minister. The SIT is headed by Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) P. Vijayan. The investigation centres on the high-profile bid by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) administration to host World Cup winners Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, for an international friendly match in Keralam. Following the the United Democratic Front’s (UDF) into power six months ago, the Sports Department flagged severe administrative lapses and financial discrepancies in the arrangements for the proposed visit, thereby prompting the investigation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SIT had earlier registered a case against event sponsor Reporter Broadcasting Company (RBC) and its managing director, Anto Augustine, who are listed as the first and second accused, respectively. The investigators have alleged that the former Minister and his aides bypassed standard departmental procedures and tender norms to extend undue financial benefits to the private broadcaster.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Messi visit row: Keralam govt. grants sanction to investigate former Sports Minister V. Abdurahiman

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 11:27:17 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The State government on Friday issued orders to accord sanction under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, to investigate former Minister for Sports, Minority Welfare and Waqf, V. Abdurahiman, along with two other former officials, over the alleged financial and procedural irregularities linked to the aborted visit of the Argentina national football team to the State. According to an order issued by the Home department, the Special Investigation Team (SIT) probing the case has been cleared to incorporate relevant sections of the Prevention of Corruption Act into its ongoing investigation. Alongside Mr. Abdurahiman, who has been named as the third accused in the case, the government has sanctioned probes against his former private secretary C. Sathyapalan, and former Kerala State Sports Council president U. Sharafali, who are the fourth and fifth accused respectively. The order follows a formal request from the State Police Chief based on a preliminary report submitted by the SIT. The government observed that an independent perusal of the SIT’s findings disclosed a prima facie case warranting an investigation into recommendations made and decisions taken by the former Minister and the officials during their tenure. The government had earlier received sanction from the Keralam Lok Bhavan to prosecute the former Minister. The SIT is headed by Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) P. Vijayan. The investigation centres on the high-profile bid by the previous Left Democratic Front (LDF) administration to host World Cup winners Argentina, led by Lionel Messi, for an international friendly match in Keralam. Following the the United Democratic Front’s (UDF) into power six months ago, the Sports Department flagged severe administrative lapses and financial discrepancies in the arrangements for the proposed visit, thereby prompting the investigation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SIT had earlier registered a case against event sponsor Reporter Broadcasting Company (RBC) and its managing director, Anto Augustine, who are listed as the first and second accused, respectively. The investigators have alleged that the former Minister and his aides bypassed standard departmental procedures and tender norms to extend undue financial benefits to the private broadcaster.

विभागीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Departmental' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

articles.title: Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector. The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids. Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said. The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines. “Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement. Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: coal / economy (general) / business (general) / minerals (general) / metal and mineral / mining / natural resources (general) / energy resources / energy and resource

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #15 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Coal auction rounds attract 85 bids; 20 first-time players enter sector

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 10:17:37 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The 16th round of commercial mine auctions put forth 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions has attracted 83 bids for 17 coal blocks with 20 first-time bidders seeking to enter commercial coal mining, signalling fresh interest in the sector. The Union Coal Ministry said on Friday that 17 blocks offered in the latest round received 83 bids. In addition, the second attempt to auction one coal block from the 15th round attracted two bids. Taking the 26 blocks covered by the auction process into account, the number of bids has quadrupled compared with the previous round, the ministry said. The 16th round of commercial coal mine auctions was launched on September 17, offering 25 blocks, comprising 21 fully explored and four partially explored mines. “Competition in the current round has been intense, with 16 of the 26 blocks attracting multiple bids. The round has also brought 20 first-time bidders into the commercial coal mining regime, a clear sign that the sector continues to draw new capital and new players,” the ministry said in a statement. Since the introduction of the commercial coal mining auction regime in June 2020, the government has auctioned 145 coal mines across 15 rounds. These mines are estimated to generate annual revenues of around ₹47,500 crore, according to government estimates.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs. Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons. Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%. While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy. “A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments. Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.” Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life. “It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save. Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / finance (general) / financial markets / stocks / stock market / investment service / investments

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #16 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 CEA flags need to align capital markets with India’s development priorities

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 09:44:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran has called for a greater role for Indian capital markets in channelising household savings into productive investments, stressing the importance of patient capital in meeting the country’s long-term development needs. Speaking at the CII Financial Summit in Mumbai, Mr. Nageswaran said sectors such as infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture and mineral exploration required long-term financing, given their extended investment horizons. Highlighting the imbalance in India’s financial markets, he pointed out that equity market capitalisation stood at around 130% of GDP, while the corporate bond market accounted for only about 16%. While acknowledging that technology had improved market access, settlement systems and transaction security, he said these advances had not necessarily translated into better outcomes for investors or the real economy. “A safer machine is not the same as a better outcome,” he said, emphasising that technological innovation should ultimately strengthen the capital market’s core function of converting savings into productive investments. Cautioning against a consumption-led economic model, Mr. Nageswaran said, “An economy that is consumption-oriented may not be the most suited one for India’s development context.” Echoing the need to promote long-term savings, Gaurav Mathur, founder and managing director of SafeGold, called for tax incentives to encourage investors to hold financial assets for longer periods. He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life. “It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save. Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / finance (general) / financial markets / stocks / stock market / investment service / investments

Technological (Adjective)
तकनीकी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Technological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

रचनात्मक — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Constructive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

He stressed that savings policies should reflect individuals’ financial circumstances and different stages of life. “It’s a matter of constructive partnership between regulators and financial intermediaries, where you incentivise long-term saving behaviour at the appropriate stages in life,” Mr. Mathur said, adding that incentives should particularly target wealthier individuals with greater capacity to save. Meanwhile, Nilesh Shah, managing director of Kotak Mahindra Asset Management Company and part-time member of the Economic Advisory Council to the Prime Minister, underscored the need to strengthen financial literacy and encourage voluntary pension savings. He said these measures were increasingly important amid uncertainties over employment and income in a technology-driven economy.

articles.title: How AI could reshape global growth and productivity
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole. A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator). There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline. One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a). Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Text and Context / economy / Artificial Intelligence / labour

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #17 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 How AI could reshape global growth and productivity

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 11:36:38 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an increase; what remains to be seen is how pervasive its impact will be across different sectors of the economy

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Many have likened the artificial intelligence (AI) phenomenon to the inventions of the steam engine or internal combustion engine in the 18th and 19th centuries, respectively. Only time can tell whether AI is epochal of that kind. In this two-part piece, we discuss the possible impact it may have on the global economy as a whole. A key impact of AI is considered to be an unprecedented rise in labour productivity. In fact, if there is one purpose AI is supposed to serve, it is enhancing labour productivity multifold. Since labour productivity is a key variable in this puzzle, consider what it constitutes of (Box 1) . It is a ratio of output and workers employed. Now this ratio can rise in three different ways — a rise in output for a given number of workers employed (rise in the numerator); a loss of jobs which leads to a fall in the denominator; more jobs are created, but the output rises faster than the jobs (while both the numerator and the denominator are rising, the numerator rises faster than the denominator). There is usually a distinction drawn between a case where there is a net loss of jobs versus one where jobs grow, but the output grows even faster. The latter is preferred over the former. Even though AI may displace white-collar workers, it may generate more jobs for the blue-collar workers, so in the net there may not be a job loss with AI adoption across the economy. However, for the argument we make below, it does not matter which of the three sources leads to a rise in productivity. Why should the rise in labour productivity matter? There are two contrasting takes on this question in the economics discipline. One which argues that productivity growth increases the growth of output in the economy. The idea is simple. Growth of output is a function of its two inputs — labour and capital. Since capital enhances the productivity of labour, the rate at which output can grow is the sum of the growth of the labour force and its productivity. So, if the workforce grows at 2% and productivity at 4%, the economy would stabilise at 6% growth over time. And if the rate of labour productivity rises, according to this framework, growth in the economy rises pari passu (Graph 1a). Between the three variables — output growth, labour growth and productivity growth — output growth adjusts to the other two. This is what Robert Solow, a celebrated economist and a Nobel laureate, showed in a seminal paper on growth theory. What he did not explain though was why and where did this labour productivity rise come from. Much later, his successors argued that the growth of labour productivity depends on investment in human capital, research and development, patent regimes, etc., what came to be known as endogenous growth theories.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Text and Context / economy / Artificial Intelligence / labour

संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।

तकनीकी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Technological' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Productivity (Noun)
उत्पादकता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Productivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Intelligence (Adjective / Verb)
बुद्धिमत्ता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Intelligence' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "How AI could reshape global growth and productivity", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'How AI could reshape global growth and productiv' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'How AI could reshape global growth and produc' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'How AI could reshape global growth and produc' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "A key expected impact of AI is an unprecedented rise in labour productivity, as its success as a technological revolution is premised on such an..." Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "How AI could reshape global growth and productivity"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Text and Context / economy / Artificial Intelligence / labour.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Text and Context / economy / Artificial Intelligence / labour." (Hinglish Arth: पाठ और संदर्भ/अर्थव्यवस्था/कृत्रिम बुद्धिमत्ता/श्रम)

articles.title: Estonia to close border with Russia, Moscow decries 'new Iron Curtain'
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government ‌said on Friday (November 20, 2026), prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures. NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year. This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to ​organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister ‌Igor Taro told a press conference. "Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is something we cannot tolerate anymore," Mr. Taro said. The Kremlin has ‌denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack. Foreign Ministry spokeswoman ​Maria Zakharova on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the ⁠closure. "Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," ‌Ms. Zakharova said. Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government. Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in ‌Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a ​majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in ⁠Europe to reach St. Petersburg a few hours' drive away.

• 1. Core Context & Background: NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on November 15 accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Estonia will close its road border crossings with Russia on security grounds for at least six months, the Baltic country's government ‌said on Friday (November 20, 2026), prompting a warning from Moscow that it would respond with political and diplomatic measures. NATO and EU member ‌Estonia on Sunday (November 15, 2026) accused Russian security services of staging an attempted ‌arson ⁠attack on an Estonian defence company, in what it said ⁠was the second such incident this year. This would help address the wider security situation and limit Russia's ability to ​organise further attacks, Estonian Interior Minister ‌Igor Taro told a press conference. "Russian security services are intimidating and trying to recruit our citizens who are travelling through our border checkpoints. This is something we cannot tolerate anymore," Mr. Taro said. The Kremlin has ‌denied any involvement in the weekend arson attack. Foreign Ministry spokeswoman ​Maria Zakharova on Friday (November 20, 2026) said that Russia would respond with political and diplomatic measures if Estonia went ahead with the ⁠closure. "Such moves are tantamount to attempts to erect a new Iron Curtain under the false pretence of some sort of threat from the East," ‌Ms. Zakharova said. Estonia, a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has five crossing points where travellers can enter or leave Russia, according to the government. Estonia's northern neighbour Finland shut its Russia border crossings in 2023, and has kept them closed since then, while southern Baltic nations Latvia and Lithuania maintain open crossings.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Thousands of people living in Estonia have family in ‌Russia or vice versa, as legacies of the Soviet era. The crossing at Narva, a ​majority Russian-speaking city on the Estonian side of the border, is also used by people travelling from further afield in ⁠Europe to reach St. Petersburg a few hours' drive away.

articles.title: Pakistan Army chief Munir vows to eliminate terrorism from country
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Pakistan overall witnessed a significant decline in terrorism-related violence during October, with attacks falling by 37%, deaths resulting from these attacks declining by 57%, and injuries decreasing by 71% compared to September, said Dawn newspaper report

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Pakistan’s Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir on Friday (November 20, 2026) expressed the “unwavering resolve” of the security forces to eliminate terrorism from the country during a visit to the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Mr. Munir, who is also the Chief of Defence Forces (CDF), said this during a visit to Miranshah in North Waziristan district, the military's media wing said in a statement. “He reaffirmed the unwavering resolve of the security forces, in close coordination with law enforcement agencies, to decisively eliminate the menace of terrorism and preserve the hard-earned peace and stability of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,” the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement. Mr. Munir also appreciated the KP police and expressed pride in its resilience and sacrifices against terrorism and Fitna-al-Khawarij. The term Fitna-al-Khawarij is used by the federal government for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. During the visit, the CDF was given a comprehensive briefing on “the prevailing security situation, ongoing intelligence-based operations [IBO] and measures being undertaken to consolidate the gains achieved through sustained counter-terrorism efforts, “ the ISPR statement said. It added that CDF Munir also interacted with officers and troops and appreciated their “high level of preparedness, professionalism and unwavering commitment". Security forces continue to carry out counterterrorism action in KP and Balochistan, the two provinces that have been particularly affected by terrorism in Pakistan. On Saturday (November 14, 2026), ISPR said four troops, including a major, were killed while 24 terrorists were killed in IBOs in Balochistan and KP’s North Waziristan.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Furthermore, last week, 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan.

articles.title: U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The U.S. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United States has frozen the assets of the leader of an ethnic armed group in Myanmar and one of his lieutenants, accusing them of facilitating cyberscammers who target Americans. Organised criminal gangs have, for years, carried out fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes from compounds in Southeast Asian nations, defrauding victims around the world of tens of billions of dollars annually. The industry is adapting its operations in the wake of much-publicised crackdowns in Myanmar and Cambodia following Chinese pressure, often dissipating into smaller facilities in new locations. The U.S. Treasury Department said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them. The DKBA is one of the myriad armed groups operating in Myanmar's borderlands, some of which have been fighting the government for decades. It has signed a ceasefire with Yangon and is accused by the United States, which earlier sanctioned the organisation, of supporting scam centres. "DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds," the U.S. Treasury said. The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026). Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The latest U.S. Treasury measures also sanctioned Zhao Hui, a China-born, naturalised Cambodian accused of running cyberscam compounds in Cambodia, and two of his companies.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 U.S. sanctions Myanmar armed group leader over scam links

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 10:48:33 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The U.S. Treasury Department said on November 19 it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The United States has frozen the assets of the leader of an ethnic armed group in Myanmar and one of his lieutenants, accusing them of facilitating cyberscammers who target Americans. Organised criminal gangs have, for years, carried out fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes from compounds in Southeast Asian nations, defrauding victims around the world of tens of billions of dollars annually. The industry is adapting its operations in the wake of much-publicised crackdowns in Myanmar and Cambodia following Chinese pressure, often dissipating into smaller facilities in new locations. The U.S. Treasury Department said on Thursday (November 19, 2026) it had imposed an asset freeze on General Saw Shwe Wah, commander-in-chief of the Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA), and one of his top officers, and had banned Americans from dealing with them. The DKBA is one of the myriad armed groups operating in Myanmar's borderlands, some of which have been fighting the government for decades. It has signed a ceasefire with Yangon and is accused by the United States, which earlier sanctioned the organisation, of supporting scam centres. "DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds," the U.S. Treasury said. The DKBA's Colonel Saw A One, responsible for security in the Three Pagodas Pass area in Karen State near the Thai border, was also designated by the U.S. on Thursday (November 19, 2026). Jason Tower, senior expert at the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, told that last week the Three Pagodas Pass region has been a "major expansion area" for scam compounds.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The latest U.S. Treasury measures also sanctioned Zhao Hui, a China-born, naturalised Cambodian accused of running cyberscam compounds in Cambodia, and two of his companies.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026). Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation. #WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. Nepali PM will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum." “Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports,” the Ministry said. This will be the Nepal Prime Minister’s first visit to India since he took charge last March. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who both visited India earlier this year, will join the delegation. Official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said Mr. Shah’s trip will be a “state visit, during which he will be accorded state honours”. “He will meet with our President and hold discussions with our Prime Minister. Given that this is a highly multifaceted relationship, the talks will cover a wide range of topics, including our development partnership, economic cooperation, and various other matters,” said Mr. Jaiswal during the biweekly media briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026). Mr. Rai said the two countries are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding covering different areas of cooperation, and a few completed projects are expected to be inaugurated following PM Balendra Shah’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Sources said the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the Uttarakhand-Nepal border, and a train route between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are slated to be opened.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Earlier this month, India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu. India’s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will be the first government representative to call on Prime Minister Shah upon his arrival on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Formal engagements will begin Monday morning with a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, followed by a visit to Rajghat, where Mr. Shah will lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial. He will then meet Prime Minister Modi at Hyderabad House, where the MoUs will be signed. He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (20 NOV)

📰 Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23

📌 Published: 20 Nov 2026, 10:39:29 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026). Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation. #WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. Nepali PM will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum." “Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports,” the Ministry said. This will be the Nepal Prime Minister’s first visit to India since he took charge last March. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who both visited India earlier this year, will join the delegation. Official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said Mr. Shah’s trip will be a “state visit, during which he will be accorded state honours”. “He will meet with our President and hold discussions with our Prime Minister. Given that this is a highly multifaceted relationship, the talks will cover a wide range of topics, including our development partnership, economic cooperation, and various other matters,” said Mr. Jaiswal during the biweekly media briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026). Mr. Rai said the two countries are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding covering different areas of cooperation, and a few completed projects are expected to be inaugurated following PM Balendra Shah’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Sources said the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the Uttarakhand-Nepal border, and a train route between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are slated to be opened.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Earlier this month, India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu. India’s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will be the first government representative to call on Prime Minister Shah upon his arrival on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Formal engagements will begin Monday morning with a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, followed by a visit to Rajghat, where Mr. Shah will lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial. He will then meet Prime Minister Modi at Hyderabad House, where the MoUs will be signed. He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Bilateral (Adjective)
द्विपक्षीय — दो देशों के बीच आपसी समझौता, व्यापार या कूटनीतिक बातचीत।
✓ Syn: Reciprocal, Two-sided, Mutual  |  ✖ Ant: Unilateral, Multilateral, One-way
Representative (Adjective)
प्रतिनिधि — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Representative' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Connectivity (Noun)
कनेक्टिविटी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Connectivity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Cooperation (Noun)
सहयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Cooperation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on Novembe' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on Nove' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on Nove' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "In his first India visit, Nepal Prime Minister is expected to sign several MoUs and inaugurate projects." (Hinglish Arth: अपनी पहली भारत यात्रा में, नेपाल के प्रधान मंत्री द्वारा कई समझौता ज्ञापनों पर हस्ताक्षर करने और परियोजनाओं का उद्घाटन करने की उम्मीद है)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Nepal PM Balendra Shah to visit India on November 22-23"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon." (Hinglish Arth: वह दोपहर बाद काठमांडू के लिए रवाना होंगे।)

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will visit India on November 22-23, the Ministry of External Affairs announced on Friday (November 20, 2026). Briefing the media in Kathmandu, Nepal’s Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai said Mr. Shah will be accompanied by a 34-member delegation. #WATCH | Kathmandu | "On the invitation of the Prime Minister of India, Nepali PM Balendra Shah will embark on a State visit to India from 22nd to 23rd November," says Nepal's Foreign Secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai. He adds, "It will be a 34-member government team that will depart from Kathmandu to New Delhi, India. During the visit, the Nepali PM will hold a delegation-level meeting on Monday with his Indian counterpart. Various projects relating to energy will be inaugurated by the two Prime Ministers. Various aspects of cooperation will be signed and exchanged. After the delegation-level talks, the two Prime Ministers will hold a joint press conference. Nepali PM will also call on the President of India, Droupadi Murmu. Nepali PM will also lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi's memorial at Rajghat. Nepali PM will also attend the Nepal-India Business Forum." “Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports,” the Ministry said. This will be the Nepal Prime Minister’s first visit to India since he took charge last March. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle and Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, who both visited India earlier this year, will join the delegation. Official spokesperson for the Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal said Mr. Shah’s trip will be a “state visit, during which he will be accorded state honours”. “He will meet with our President and hold discussions with our Prime Minister. Given that this is a highly multifaceted relationship, the talks will cover a wide range of topics, including our development partnership, economic cooperation, and various other matters,” said Mr. Jaiswal during the biweekly media briefing on Friday (November 20, 2026). Mr. Rai said the two countries are expected to sign several memorandums of understanding covering different areas of cooperation, and a few completed projects are expected to be inaugurated following PM Balendra Shah’s meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Sources said the Dharchula Bridge, the land port of Banbasa at the Uttarakhand-Nepal border, and a train route between Janakpur and Gorakhpur are slated to be opened.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Earlier this month, India’s Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri visited Kathmandu. India’s External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar will be the first government representative to call on Prime Minister Shah upon his arrival on Sunday (November 22, 2026). Formal engagements will begin Monday morning with a ceremonial reception at the Rashtrapati Bhavan, followed by a visit to Rajghat, where Mr. Shah will lay a wreath at Mahatma Gandhi’s memorial. He will then meet Prime Minister Modi at Hyderabad House, where the MoUs will be signed. He will leave for Kathmandu later that afternoon.

articles.title: Bangladesh hit by fresh arson attacks in political unrest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Police said 124 people linked to the Awami League had been arrested in the capital Dhaka over the past 24 hours, without providing further details

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Fresh arson attacks erupted in Bangladesh on Friday (November 20, 2026) as authorities restored communications with the hometown of convicted former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, after days of unrest over her planned return from exile. Ms. Hasina, 79, has vowed to return to Bangladesh in December from India, despite being sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown during the 2024 uprising that ousted her. Ms. Hasina's former ruling party, the Awami League, whose activities are now banned, called for strikes this week to mark the anniversary of the day Ms. Hasina received her death sentence. Hundreds of paramilitary troops have been deployed to contain the unrest, in which at least three people have been killed. A petrol bomb was hurled at the residence of a junior Foreign Minister, Humaiun Kobir, in the northeastern city of Sylhet on Friday (November 20, 2026), police said. Mr. Kobir said Dhaka would deal with attacks "very firmly". "It is not possible to bring back a 'fled terrorist' by throwing petrol bombs," he told reporters on Friday (November 20, 2026). Ms. Hasina has said repeatedly she wants to return next month, telling AFP in an email this week that she was "fully aware" she could be hanged. Attackers also set fire to the home of a former junior Foreign Minister from the Awami League in Rajshahi on Thursday (November 19, 2026).
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Protesters wielding machetes also torched a police station in Gopalganj, Ms. Hasina's political stronghold, the same day. Communications have since been restored.
